ops.viejo: The control records SBS showed in 2020 also place the freighter in the zone: around 18:04 the controller warned it that it might enter it, and the plane entered three minutes later, around 18:07, six minutes before the first shooting given in the telegram; according to those records, it kept its course for about 30 minutes.
ops.nuevo: In 2020 SBS showed the recording of the freighter's exchanges with air traffic control, without saying where it had obtained it. Between 18:04 and 18:09 the controller warned the crew that, if they held that course, they could enter the prohibited zone. The program placed the first shooting at 18:12, three minutes after that warning, and the second at 18:39: if both were aimed at the freighter, it would still have been on its course half an hour later. The telegrams give other times, 18:13 and 18:32.

ops.viejo: El Proyecto Colorado recogió además el aviso del capitán de un pesquero, a unas 16 millas, que había visto tres luces rojas intermitentes e inmóviles sobre el agua y cuatro puntos en su radar, que tomó por buques de la Marina, y una luz que subió en vertical y que tomó por un helicóptero. Como la posición que dio quedaba a unas 175 millas náuticas del lugar, el informe concluyó que ambos episodios no parecían relacionados.
ops.nuevo: El Proyecto Colorado recogió además el aviso del capitán de un pesquero que estaba a unas 16 millas del lugar de los avistamientos. Desde la puesta del sol hasta las 23:00, él y su tripulación habían visto tres luces rojas intermitentes e inmóviles sobre el agua y cuatro puntos en su radar, que tomó por buques de la Marina; hacia las 23:00, una de las luces subió en vertical y la tomó por un helicóptero. Como la posición que dio para esos objetos quedaba a unas 175 millas náuticas del lugar, el informe concluyó que ambos episodios no parecían relacionados; no explica cómo encaja esa distancia con las 16 millas.

ops.viejo: The Colorado Project also recorded the report of a fishing-boat captain some 16 miles away who had seen three stationary, flashing red lights on the water and four blips on his radar, which he took for naval vessels, and a light rising that he took for a helicopter. Since the position he gave was about 175 nautical miles from the site, the report concluded the two episodes did not appear to be related.
ops.nuevo: The Colorado Project also recorded the report of a fishing-boat captain who had been about 16 miles from the site of the sightings. From sundown until 11:00 p.m. he and his crew had seen three stationary, flashing red lights on the water and four blips on his radar, which he took for naval vessels; at about 11:00 p.m. one of the lights went straight up, and he took it for a helicopter. Since the position he gave for those objects was about 175 nautical miles from the site, the report concluded the two episodes did not appear to be related; it does not explain how that distance squares with the 16 miles.
